The ERD proposed Customer(customer_id, name, address, contact_details, kyc_details), Account(account_number, account_type, account_balance, account_status), Transaction(transaction_id, transaction_type, transaction_date, transaction_amount, transaction_status), Loan(loan_id, loan_type, loan_amount, interest_rate, repayment_schedule), Credit(credit_limit, credit_utilization, credit_score, credit_status), Risk(risk_id, risk_type, risk_level, risk_status), Compliance(compliance_id, compliance_type, compliance_status, compliance_deadline), Treasury(investment_portfolio, cash_reserves, forex_transactions), Business Intelligence(revenue, profitability, market_share, kpi), and Integration/API(api_endpoints, api_keys, integration_status). Stated relationships: a customer has many accounts and loans; an account belongs to one customer and has many transactions; each transaction belongs to one account; a loan belongs to one customer and an account can have many loans; Credit, Risk, Compliance, Treasury, Business Intelligence, and Integration/API each belong to one customer.

On 2023-05-22, the assistant first said the ERD’s normalization could not be confirmed without knowing its functional dependencies. In its step-by-step response, the assistant assumed each table had no functional dependencies beyond its primary key, added customer_id and other foreign keys, and claimed loan_type and interest_rate were transitively dependent on loan_amount, splitting them into Loan_Type and Interest_Rate tables. When asked to continue through 5NF, the assistant also split Treasury into Treasury, Investment, Cash, and Forex_Transaction tables, and Integration/API into Integration, API_Endpoint, API_Key, and Integration_Status tables. It then claimed the resulting tables were in 3NF and 5NF, asserting there were no further dependencies to decompose. The assistant’s stated dependencies and 5NF conclusion were based on assumptions rather than enough information in the ERD to establish them.
